headline: Quiet, chilly weather with possible frost early in the week; only light rain and mountain flurries possible Thursday into Friday.
summary: Western Washington stays quiet, with a storm system passing well offshore and sending mostly high clouds. Monday morning lows should be in the mid 30s from Olympia south along the I-5 corridor and in the mid 40s elsewhere. Tuesday morning is a few degrees colder, so frost is possible in the south Puget Sound, the Chehalis Valley, the Cascades, and valleys. Patchy morning fog is possible early in the week, most likely in valleys and other spots that often get fog. Later in the week a weak system may bring light rain Thursday into Friday. If precipitation does develop, snow levels could fall to around 4,000 to 4,500 feet, so a few light snow flurries are possible at those elevations and higher. Forecasters do not expect much impactful weather. The position of a low pressure area near California becomes less certain by Friday into the weekend. The coast may see a larger swell of about 10 to 12 feet offshore around Thursday.
changes: Early discussions called for dry weather with morning fog and only a weak front late in the week. Later ones put more emphasis on chilly lows and possible frost Monday and Tuesday mornings, and added the coastal swell. Rain and flurry chances for Thursday into Friday stayed light and uncertain.
